findings.title: "Read-side over 300's write path" is contradicted by what 300 actually persists
findings.description:
Line 46 says 300 persisted results "as self-describing (provenance) precisely so 320 could consume them", and line 102 forbids changing the judging path. The code does not support that premise:

- **No stable result identity; records are overwritten.** `save_review_result` writes to `{index}-review.{template}.{slice_name}.md` with `write_text` (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:282-299`). The shipped `judge-cycle.yaml` loops the judge up to 3 times, so each iteration overwrites the last. The only timestamp is a `YYYYMMDD` date. Line 75's requirement to "attach unambiguously to the specific persisted judge result" has nothing to attach to, and line 67's trend has no history.
- **Provenance is not persisted.** `persistence.py:147` states it is never emitted. `ReviewAction` sets provenance only on the in-memory `ActionResult` (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:296`), and `pipeline/state.py` hoists `score` but contains no provenance field.
- **Judge configuration is not recorded.** Line 79 fixes "keyed by judge configuration (template identity/version, model)". The record has a template name and a model string only. Templates have no version field, and a user-directory template can replace a built-in under the same name (`review/templates/__init__.py:200-202`). The thresholds that produced the verdict are not stored either.
- **Persistence is best-effort.** A save failure is a WARNING and the gate still proceeds (`review.py:244-280`). Without `slice_info` the record is written with `slice: unknown`, `project: unknown`, slice `0` (`persistence.py:126-128`). The sampling frame therefore has holes and unjoinable rows.

All of this must be captured at judge time; none of it can be reconstructed by a read-side layer. Fix the document: replace the read-only principle with "additive write-path changes, owned by 320's keystone slice", and enumerate them:

- a unique result id, with append instead of overwrite;
- persisted provenance and the thresholds in effect;
- a template content hash and the resolved model id;
- a content hash or git SHA of the judged artifact.

Amend the non-goal at line 102 to match. Otherwise slice design inherits work the architecture prohibits.

findings.title: Dispersion relies on a "multi-sample option" that does not exist
findings.description:
Line 81 says "The execution machinery exists — 300's multi-sample option and 140's `fan_out`". Lines 62 and 109 of the same document call multi-sample "300 Future Work 1", and it is unchecked in `300-slices`. The fan-in reducers (`pipeline/intelligence/fan_in/reducers.py`) either gather branches or return the first PASS; there is no median or score reducer.

Two further gaps:

- A `review` step inside `fan_out` would write every branch to the same review file path, because the filename has no model or branch component. Multi-judge runs would clobber each other in the per-project record.
- "Accept dispersion data opportunistically (when multi-sample ran anyway)" requires that multi-sample keep each sample's score, not only the reduced median. That constrains unbuilt 300 work and nobody owns it.

Say plainly that only `fan_out` exists, and decide whether 320 builds the calibration-run path itself or takes 300 FW1 as a prerequisite with a "retain per-leg scores" requirement.

findings.title: Calibration grain is finer than the threshold locus it feeds
findings.description:
Calibration is keyed by artifact level × judge configuration including model (lines 48, 79). Thresholds resolve from template default and step override only (`resolve_thresholds`, `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/judge.py:41-57`); there is no model dimension. The judge model is a pipeline param (`review-model` in `judge-cycle.yaml`) that can be changed per run.

A floor loosened on evidence earned by model X therefore silently applies when the step runs model Y. That is the "moving thresholds on noise" failure line 52 warns against.

Two related gaps:

- Template defaults are package data shipped with squadron. Operator-specific calibration cannot live there; only step overrides or user-directory template copies remain, and the document does not choose.
- The feedback slice (line 95, "documented, evidence-floored path") does not say whether its output is a report, a generated override snippet, or a command.

Either state that a calibrated threshold is only valid for the configuration that earned it and specify how the engine detects a mismatch at gate time, or commit to the additive change that lets thresholds be scoped by model.

findings.title: The human oracle's verdict is never defined, and it determines the keystone schema
findings.description:
"Their verdict is recorded against the judge's result" (line 67) does not say what the operator records. The options are agree/disagree with the judge's verdict, an independent PASS/CONCERNS/FAIL, or a score. This is not slice detail:

- The judge's verdict is a projection of its score through the very thresholds calibration will move. Agree/disagree data is invalidated every time a threshold changes and cannot be replayed against candidate thresholds.
- "X overreaches, Y rubber-stamps" (lines 20, 32) needs signed disagreement. Binary agreement cannot produce it.
- Recommending a floor requires the human's independent categorical call paired with the judge's raw score.
- "Spot-checks a judge call" implies the operator sees the judge's verdict first. That anchors the human and inflates agreement.

Commit here: the sample is an independent human verdict, stored against the raw score, with agreement recomputed under whatever thresholds are being evaluated. State whether capture is blind.

findings.title: "Normal course of work" sampling cannot see the results that matter for loosening a gate
findings.description:
Lines 34 and 42 require sampling to be opportunistic and inline. Under 300 the operator only meets judge results that escalate. PASS results auto-advance unseen, yet the false-pass rate is exactly what must be bounded before a floor is lowered. Line 75 acknowledges sample bias but defers it as "slice-level"; the conflict with the "no dedicated labeling" principle is architectural.

A second gap is that the judged artifact is not preserved. In the judge cycle the fix dispatch mutates the artifact between iterations. Per 300 Future Work 5, `commit` cannot be a loop-body step. A later spot-check therefore judges a different document from the one the judge scored.

The architecture should fix a random-sample quota of auto-passed results, presented at a natural stopping point. It should also require an artifact snapshot or hash on every sampled result.

findings.title: The mandated grain and the evidence floor are arithmetically incompatible with "a handful" of samples
findings.description:
The document fixes per-level reporting (line 48), per-configuration keying with no blending across "incompatible" configurations (line 79), and a minimum-evidence floor (line 77). It expects "a handful" of samples (line 52).

By the rule of three, bounding a disagreement rate below 10% at 95% confidence needs about 30 clean samples per cell. With 3 levels and 2 models that is roughly 180 spot-checks. Every cell resets on any template edit or model change. A single operator will never clear the floor, so the "conservative tax" of line 61 becomes permanent by construction.

Missing decisions:

- A definition of "incompatible", and a pooling rule (for example, pool across template revisions that leave the rubric and bands unchanged).
- A rough order-of-magnitude floor, so feasibility can be judged now.
- Trend scope. Agreement trend at this n is noise; restrict trend to judge score distributions, which need no human labels.

Separately, only two judge templates exist (`judge.slice-vs-arch`, `judge.tasks-vs-slice`). The arch-vs-concept level in line 30 has no judge to calibrate, and no slice authors one.

findings.title: The storage home is the keystone decision and is deferred; the named candidate cannot meet the stated requirement
findings.description:
Line 87 introduces cross-project aggregation as "a new requirement" and leaves the store to slice design, naming 280 as a candidate (also line 112). Three problems:

- 280's store is per-project (`{project_root}/.squadron/artifacts.db` in `280-arch`), so it cannot aggregate across projects.
- 280 is not started and sits behind 260 and 240, and the initiative plan declares 320 independent of 280.
- "Squadron-managed projects" (lines 69, 96) has no backing concept. There is no project registry in `src/`; squadron operates per working directory.

The stack has no database today; records are markdown frontmatter in the repo and run-state JSON under `~/.config/squadron/runs/`. Decide at this level, and take the lightest option: append-only records beside the reviews in each repo, with reports given an explicit list of project roots. Drop the 280 candidate and the implied registry.

findings.title: "Audit-findings-per-project drops" is not a valid measure with the skill as shipped
The audit harness has no execution path in the current stack
findings.description:
The audit is a Claude Code slash command. 340-arch is explicit that "Claude Code's existing slash command system handles invocation unchanged"; squadron only copies the file, and the pack is opt-in. The protocol uses `TodoWrite`, Task subagents and shell tooling (`pip-audit`, `vulture`, `git log`), takes 5–20 minutes, and writes its own `analysis/nnn-analysis.*.md` file.

"Run the audit across squadron-managed projects" therefore needs decisions the document does not make:

- How a slash-command skill is executed headlessly: as a dispatch prompt on an SDK profile with Bash and Task permitted, or as a new action.
- What happens on non-SDK profiles, which have no tool use until 260 lands.
- Whether the harness requires the pack to be installed or reads the bundled source directly.

The frontmatter `dependencies: [100, 140, 300]` also omits 340, although lines 22, 63 and 111 depend on it and 340-arch names 320 as its primary consumer.

findings.title: "Two oracles, one metrology shape — built once" is an abstraction the two data shapes do not share
findings.description:
Judge calibration is paired-rater agreement on one item: human verdict against judge score, keyed by level and judge configuration. The audit baseline is single-rater finding counts per project over time, with category and severity. They share only "persist a record, aggregate, print n".

Committing to a single reporting layer before either exists invites a generic verdict-record abstraction that fits neither. Cut the shared-layer commitment and build two small reporters; extract common code only if duplication appears. The speculative "interface parity if other surfaces are added" clause at line 75 can be dropped for the same reason.

findings.title: The `criteria` example contradicts the read-only principle and is not aggregable
findings.description: Line 46 says 320 "populates or reads" the reserved `criteria` map. The judge templates already populate it, and 320 populating it would be a write in the judging path. The keys are model-chosen free text (`<criterion name>` in `judge-tasks-vs-slice.yaml:37-39`), so per-criterion values cannot be joined across runs without fixing the key set in the templates.

findings.title: Scope matches plan entry 10; nothing assigned is dropped
findings.description: Both oracles, per-level calibration, dispersion and the pre-emption prompt are all in the plan entry and all present. The overweight items are named in the findings above: the 280 coupling, the shared reporting layer, and agreement trend.
